transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Moreno (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood SRE), Marta Ruiz (CTO - KestrelHealth), Jon Park (Platform Eng), Aditi Singh (ML Eng), Evan Lee (Product), Chris (legal - partial)
Links: kernel-choice spreadsheet (redwood.com/shared/kernels-ksl), hedging runbook (redwood.com/shared/hedge-runbook), security note (redwood.com/sec/kestrel)

Summary:
Quick POC weekly check-in focused on ttft/streaming hedge plan and operational handoff for the upcoming Dedicated baseline run. Customer is seeing intermittent microburst latency spikes at peak hours, wants plan to reduce first-token time and streaming jitter while preserving cost profile. Discussed kernel choice tradeoffs, prefix/KV caching, and routing hedges. Agreed on artifacts to exchange and a target on-site Dedicated run in ~3 weeks.

Topics covered:
- Current TTFT and streaming tail symptoms
- Sequence length distribution and quantization impact
- Kernel selection heuristic + hedging policy options
- Network and VPC considerations for Dedicated run
- Security checklist and next steps

Action items: see metadata list above

Transcript body:
00:00 Samira: Alright folks, thanks for joining. Hi Marta, thanks for making time. We got about 55 minutes, big items — microburst hedging plan, kernel choices for the Dedicated run and ops handoff. Luca you wanna kick off with the perf summary?
00:18 Luca: Yeah sure. So we re-ran the microburst profiles with the latest stream runtime, trying the hybrid kernel path - basically toggling between the tensor-fused kernel and the aten-like fallback. We saw median ttft drop by ~22% on our samples but microburst tail still shows 95th spikes at about 2x baseline when concurrency jumps. There's noise in the trace because the kay-vee cash — sorry, KV cache — warm-up pattern is uneven on variable seqlens.
00:44 Marta: When you say hybrid kernel path are you referring to the rule where short sequences go to the fused kernel and long ones to the fallback?
00:52 Luca: Exactly, short <= 64 tokens on fused, >64 use the fallback for better memory behavior. But that threshold is a tunable; for your distribution — Aditi's numbers — we may want to nudge it to 80. There's a tradeoff: fused is faster single-token but uses a hot path that can cause cache contention under bursts.
01:14 Aditi: Our prompt lengths are weirdly bimodal — half under 40, some flows with long context, ~20% over 300. Most streaming completions are under 120 tokens though. I can add a bucketed distribution to the trace.
01:28 Jon: The spikes correlate with our batch fan-out during morning syncs. We often see a spike when mobile clients simultaneously fetch context + assistant generation.
01:37 Samira: Good color. The hedging plan I'm proposing is: primary path uses the fused kernel for short requests, but when queue length or observed P50 latency exceeds threshold we hedge with a secondary route — either a quantized variant on cheaper hardware or a conservative kernel path. Luca?
01:57 Luca: Yep that's what our hedging runbook outlines. Two practical hedges: 1) kernel hedge — fall back to the aten-like kernel on the same instance to avoid microburst thrash; 2) variant hedge — route to a quantized 4-bit model copy on a pool with more headroom. Variant hedge has cost implications but lowers tail. In practice we set a short ttl and cancel the slower of the two.
02:23 Marta: How does cancelation work? If we launch two requests does that double tokens billing?
02:30 Priya: So billing depends on how you count. For the pilot Dedicated run Redwood will instrument token accounting so we can attribute hedged duplications in the pilot and show amortized unit cost. We also have fast-cancel where the second call stops generating as soon as the first returns; backend still incurs compute for started work but we can measure net cost delta.
02:51 Evan: Is there a chance hedging increases variability rather than reduce it?
02:56 Luca: If thresholds aren't tuned, yes. That's why we want to run a short A/B sweep with your traffic trace. We'll sample the hedged behavior at different thresholds and pick the sweet spot where 95/99th improves with minimal cost delta.
03:12 Aditi: I'll prepare the 48-hour anonymized trace — includes prompt lengths and timestamps. Note: some prompts include long system instructions we strip out.
03:21 Samira: Perfect. Jon can you comment on the VPC/network side for the Dedicated run? Any firewall or peering blockers?
03:29 Jon: We need to open a couple ports for health and metrics and allow peering with Redwood's private subnet — I'll send a diagram. Also curious about egress costs if we spin up a quantized variant on a different region.
03:40 Samira: We'll document region impact. For the Dedicated baseline we recommend colocated in the same region. We'll also provide an autoscale policy suggestion to shrink the headroom during off-peak.
03:51 Chris (legal): Quick question — encryption at rest for the custom model variants, is that covered?
03:57 Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports KMS-managed keys. We'll attach Redwood's note but for Private you manage keys. For Dedicated we can enable CMK so logs and model artifacts are encrypted.
04:08 Marta: We need SOC2 + retention notes before the on-site run.
04:12 Samira: We'll send the SOC2 summary and the encryption/KMS docs by Friday.
04:17 Luca: Back to kernels — one nuance: quantization level interacts with kernel choice. 4-bit quant tends to work well on the fused path but some kernels have better latency with 8-bit depending on attention implementation. There's no one-size.
04:34 Aditi: Did you see quality delta with 4-bit during the last runs? We ran evals on a developer prompt set and saw small n-gram differences but not material.
04:43 Luca: Correct, eval delta was <1% for the conversational prompts, but for code-gen or long-context summarization you can see regression. We should lock down a prompt set for Kestrel to validate quality before committing.
04:56 Evan: Is there a recommended rollback if quality drops in production?
05:00 Samira: Yes, rollback policy's part of the rollout: automatic fallback to previous model variant plus isary — sorry Canary — plus immediate telemetry alerting. We'll share the rollout doc.
05:11 Marta: On the hedging thresholds, can you suggest defaults? We're worried about oscillation if we set them too low.
05:20 Luca: Start with queue length > 8 OR P50 > 70ms for hedging to kernel; route to variant hedge when queue > 16 or P95 > 250ms. Those numbers come from our lab runs but we'll validate with your trace.
05:36 Jon: For network jitter, do you measure RTT at the instance side or at the load balancer?
05:41 Priya: We look at both. For microbursts often it's internal scheduling/kv warmup; external RTT matters but is usually smaller. We'll instrument at the LB and per-GPU worker.
05:53 Marta: Okay, I'd like a quick step-by-step for the on-site Dedicated run — what do you need from us?
05:59 Samira: Good question — high level: 1) Provide trace and seqlen distribution; 2) Allow VPC peering and designated ports; 3) Approve a short Dedicated window for load test; 4) Give a prompt set for quality evals. We'll send a checklist.
06:16 Aditi: I'll assemble the trace and prompt evals. Question: are you able to run kernel experiments without redeploying models each time?
06:23 Luca: Yes, our runtime supports dynamic kernel selection flags per route. We can toggle the fused threshold and the hedging TTL at runtime; in worst case we can redeploy but it's usually a config flip.
06:34 Evan: Can you show us a dashboard of how hedging would look historically?
06:39 Samira: We can synth a replay from your trace and demo the hedging overlay in Console, showing dual requests, cancellation, and token accounting. We'll include that in the runbook.
06:50 Marta: On cost — if hedging uses a quantized variant on a separate pool, how do we understand cost per 1k requests?
06:56 Priya: We'll run an amortized cost calc during the pilot and produce a per-1k request estimate across scenarios. The kernel hedge is lower cost than variant hedge because it stays on the same instance.
07:08 Luca: One more note on prefix caching — for your flows where context is reused we can enable prefix cache to cut tokens and amortize KV warmup. But cache TTL and invalidation need product alignment.
07:20 Aditi: We do have a lot of reused context for session-based assistants; TTL of 10 minutes would help a lot.
07:25 Samira: We'll add prefix cache config examples to the runbook.
07:30 Marta: Any concerns about legal/data residency if we route hedges out-of-region?
07:35 Chris (legal): Yes, we need hard guarantees. If hedging routes to a different region we need documented data flow and a compliance review. For pilot keep everything in-region.
07:44 Samira: Understood — we'll keep pilot region-local and document that variant pool is also in-region.
07:48 Jon: Regarding logging — we need to ensure PII is not captured in traces.
07:53 Priya: We'll provide instructions for redaction and only ingest anonymized traces. Redwood's data retention policy for pilot will be short lived and adjustable.
07:59 Aditi: After the Dedicated run, can we get a per-route cost/latency breakdown?
08:04 Luca: Yes, Console will show token-level cost, per-route latency histograms and hedging overlays. We'll export the baseline and the hedged runs.
08:12 Samira: Ok we're nearing time. Quick recap? Luca, can you do a short recap of technical next steps?
08:18 Luca: Sure. 1) We'll run a replay against your 48h trace and sweep hedging thresholds in staging; 2) We'll prepare kernel threshold suggestions (start 64->80 tuning) and quant profiles for 4-bit and 8-bit; 3) We'll produce an autoscale policy for the Dedicated window; 4) We'll demo hedging overlay in Console.
08:39 Marta: And from Kestrel side: we'll provide the trace, prompt set, approve VPC peering, and confirm Dedicated run window. Also want the SOC2 and KMS docs.
08:51 Samira: Great. Final items — I'll email the hedging runbook and kernel spreadsheet right after this meeting, Luca will follow up with the Dedicated config. We'll aim to have all artifacts by 2026-10-22.
08:59 Evan: Sounds good. Anything else?
09:01 Chris: No, that's it for legal side.
09:03 Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll send calendar invite for the Dedicated run prep meeting. Bye.

End of transcript
